scope.description: Hand-researched deepening pass for the English WotC-era bounded Jumbo / oversized subset, emphasizing physical-format identification, movie and magazine distribution, BattleZone / Best of Game Winner jumbo prize memory, and the boundary between modeled early rows and the much larger later Jumbo universe.
not_claiming: complete WotC-era Jumbo coverage beyond the bounded local rows

sources.title: Local English supplemental WotC catalog: Jumbo cards - WoC-era bounded subset
TCGdex English Jumbo set metadata endpoint

claims.text: The local catalog dates the bounded English WotC-era Jumbo subset from February 2000 through July 2003, beginning with the Top Deck Magazine Pikachu row and ending with the BattleZone / Best of Game Winner Jumbo rows before the later Nintendo/e-League sequence.

The local catalog classifies the release as a jumbo_partial_bounded_subset: a supplemental oversized-card format rather than a standard playable expansion, theme deck, or complete modern Jumbo archive.

The local release models 10 rows, and the boundary proof classifies the same 10 source rows as modeled_wotc_prefix while excluding 323 later merchandise-era rows, 26 later source-set rows, 25 modern 25th Anniversary rows, and 6 post-WotC Nintendo/e-League rows.

The modeled rows preserve three early oversized routes: Top Deck Magazine's February 2000 Pikachu, the July 2000 Warner Bros. Pokemon The Movie 2000 triple-bird promotion, and BattleZone / Best of Game Winner Jumbo rows from December 2002 through July 2003.

The boundary proof keeps the full TCGdex Jumbo bucket from being treated as a WotC-era set: later 25th Anniversary, Nintendo/e-League, later source-set, and later merchandise-era oversized rows are deliberately outside this release dossier.

The local attention structure is led by Pikachu 58/102, Articuno, Moltres, and Zapdos, Electabuzz Best 1, Hitmonchan Best 2, Rocket's Scizor Best 4, Rocket's Sneasel Best 5, Dark Ivysaur Best 6, Dark Venusaur Best 7, Rocket's Mewtwo Best 8, and Rocket's Hitmonchan Best 9.

The local supplemental source rows do not provide illustrator names for this slice. That absence is itself load-bearing: agents must not fill artist authority from regular-size memory when the cataloged object is an oversized promotional format.

This bounded Jumbo slice matters because Pokemon cards are no longer only things shuffled into a deck; they become wall-sized mascot memory, movie-promotion spectacle, magazine reward, and organized-play prize evidence. The card shape remains familiar, but the use changes: display, announcement, trophy, proof-of-being-there.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, binder photo, or agent search result names an English Jumbo, oversized, Top Deck, Warner Bros., or Best of Game Winner Jumbo card.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Confirm oversized Jumbo physical format and exact distribution route before treating a familiar card name or art lineage as this catalog row.
steps: Ask whether the object is an oversized / Jumbo physical card; a regular-size card with the same name, art lineage, number, or Winner stamp is not this row.
Preserve the source route: Top Deck Magazine, Warner Bros. Pokemon The Movie 2000, or BattleZone / Best of Game Winner Jumbo.
Preserve the printed number or absence of number exactly, including 58/102, None, and Best 1 through Best 9.
Check the boundary proof before importing later Jumbo rows; the full TCGdex Jumbo bucket is not this bounded WotC-era subset.
Request size-bearing evidence for transactional use, such as a photo beside a regular card, ruler, sleeve/page, or other scale reference.

narrative.human_title: Jumbo cards - WoC-era bounded subset: oversized memory before it becomes a bucket
narrative.why_it_matters: Jumbo is where the card stops pretending it belongs in a deck and starts acting like a poster, prize, magazine insert, or movie object. This bounded WotC-era slice is small on purpose: Top Deck Pikachu, the Warner Bros. triple birds, and the BattleZone / Best of Game Winner Jumbos are allowed to speak before the later Jumbo universe floods the room. The agent's job is to keep the physical format visible, because the art may look familiar while the object is doing a different job.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Pikachu as the 58/102 Jumbo row in the bounded English WotC-era Jumbo subset.
The local collector signal preserves Top Deck Magazine (February 2000) and Base Set as the source route for this oversized Pikachu row.
The supplemental source row does not provide an illustrator for this Jumbo slice; the dossier deliberately leaves the artist field empty rather than borrowing from regular Base Set memory.
The local row carries special identification instructions requiring Jumbo / oversized physical-format confirmation and exclusion of regular-size cards or later jumbo reissues.

Pikachu 58/102 is the cleanest trap in the slice: everyone recognizes Base Set Pikachu, which is exactly why the agent must slow down and ask whether this is the Top Deck oversized object. The mascot has been enlarged into a magazine-era display artifact.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A user or seller says Pikachu 58/102, Base Set Pikachu, Top Deck Pikachu, or Jumbo Pikachu.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Confirm this is the oversized Top Deck Magazine Jumbo Pikachu, not a regular Base Set Pikachu or later oversized reissue.
steps: Require evidence that the physical object is oversized / Jumbo.
Preserve the Top Deck Magazine (February 2000) route.
Preserve the printed 58/102 number without treating the row as ordinary Base Set inventory.
Exclude regular-size Base Set Pikachu and 25th Anniversary First Partner oversized Pikachu unless a separate catalog row is selected.

card_highlights.collector_texture_note: A familiar Pikachu face becomes a format problem: for this row, the important first question is not 'which Pikachu?' but 'what size object is in the hand?'

narrative.human_title: Pikachu 58/102: the mascot made too large for the deck
narrative.why_it_matters: This is the row that teaches the whole Jumbo lesson. A regular Base Set Pikachu can make the eye relax; the oversized Top Deck route should make the agent wake up. The charm is familiar, but the object belongs to magazine/display culture, not ordinary binder-page Base Set.

card_highlights.rarity_signal: Warner Bros. Pokemon The Movie 2000 promotion (July 2000)

narrative.human_title: Articuno, Moltres, and Zapdos: the movie made oversized
narrative.why_it_matters: This Jumbo feels like a lobby poster that learned how to be a card. The useful collector memory is not only the three legendary birds, but the Warner Bros. Movie 2000 route: spectacle, distribution, and format all have to arrive together.
